result.description: Intapp DealCloud: CRM and deal management platform for private capital, investment banking and professional services firms.
result.auth_detail: Public REST API: OAuth2 Client Credentials (token endpoint POST {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token, client_id plus API key/secret, scopes such as data and user_management). Bearer token expires after 15 minutes. The MCP server uses a separate per-user OAuth flow with discovery and no client ID or secret.
result.access_detail: No public signup, free tier or sandbox found. Each DealCloud site has its own API base URL and Swagger page. Credentials come from API Keys settings inside an existing, sales-led customer site, so an admin of a licensed tenant has to issue them. I did not fetch the API Keys page, so how credentials are issued is partly inferred from integrator docs.
result.api_notes: REST areas: Authentication, User Management, Schema, Data, Backups, Publications, Relationship Intelligence and Schema Contracts, about 60 doc sub-pages. Per-site Swagger. The GraphQL-style query tools (introspect, execute_query) appear in the MCP server's tool list. The REST docs do not state GraphQL support.
result.blocker: No self-serve signup or developer sandbox. API credentials exist only inside a licensed DealCloud customer site, so building and testing needs a customer or partner tenant.

evidence.quote: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token
Tokens expire after 900 seconds (15 minutes) and must be refreshed by repeating the flow.
Each DealCloud site provides an interactive Swagger page for testing API calls.
This site provides a comprehensive overview of our REST APIs, their capabilities, and available endpoints.
DealCloud MCP uses OAuth to authenticate, letting AI assistants connect on behalf of an individual user.
To enable write tools, go to **Tools > MCP Servers**, edit the MCP Server, and turn on the **Enable Write Tools** toggle.
